title: Hosted endpoint peakhunt runbook - 15s buckets
content:
Context:
This doc captures an experimental runbook and working notes for a new "peakhunt" workflow aimed at discovering short, intense microbursts in Hosted API traffic using 15-second buckets. Motivation is to find "needle" bursts that traditional 5m/15m aggregation misses, quantify their tokens/sec and QPS signatures, and set explicit headroom targets per-region and per-GPU-family.

Goals (high level):
- Uncover microburst profiles (15s granularity) across regions and model classes.
- Derive per-region headroom targets in tokens/sec and QPS with explicit safety factors for 15s, 1m, and 5m windows.
- Produce operational runbook: pre-warm, routing fallback, and rapid scale triggers for 15s bursts.
- Provide a reproducible analysis pipeline and replay harness for synthetic stress tests.

Assumptions and inputs:
- Historical full-token event stream available (sampled) for last 180 days.
- Model mix: 50% conversational (avg seq 180 tokens), 30% completion (avg seq 60 tokens), 20% embeddings/short (avg seq 16 tokens).
- GPU families in play: A100-80GB (dense chat), H100-80GB (low-latency high-throughput), T4/RTX (burst overflow).
- Target SLO: p99 latency < 1.2s for short completions, p95 < 3s for long chats.

Methodology overview:
1) Re-bucket raw events into 15s sliding windows (step 5s) to surface microbursts.
2) Compute per-window tokens/sec, QPS, average seq length, and hot-model concentration (fraction of requests to top-5 models).
3) Characterize burst shapes: rise time, decay time, peak:baseline ratio, model concentration.
4) Map peak tokens/sec to GPU slices using conservative per-GPU token throughput estimates derived from bench runs.
5) Apply safety multipliers: baseline headroom = observed 99.9th percentile * 1.15 (experimentation), emergency trigger = observed * 1.5.

Representative findings (sample from APAC, 90-day lookback):
- Observed 15s p99.9 tokens/sec (APAC-northeast): 1,240k tokens/sec.
- Observed 15s median tokens/sec (APAC-northeast): 95k tokens/sec.
- Peak bursts are highly concentrated: top-1 model accounts for 62% of tokens in peak windows (chat-heavy event).

Mapping to GPU capacity (example throughput assumptions):
- H100-80GB (chat-tuned): estimated sustained token throughput (15s window) = 140k tokens/sec per card when sequence reuse is high (long-chat).
- A100-80GB (dense batching): 110k tokens/sec per card.
- T4/replicas (spill): 35k tokens/sec per card.

Example headroom calc (APAC-northeast):
- observed p99.9 = 1,240,000 tokens/sec -> conservative headroom target = 1,240,000 * 1.15 = 1,426,000 tokens/sec.
- Map to cards: if using H100 primary fleet -> 1,426,000 / 140,000 ≈ 10.2 -> round up to 12 cards (reserve for affinity/placement).
- Emergency trigger threshold = 1,240,000 * 1.5 = 1,860,000 tokens/sec -> 14 H100 equivalents (page SRE).

QPS translation (approx):
- For mixed model mix average tokens/request = (0.5*180 + 0.3*60 + 0.2*16) = 114 tokens/request.
- So 1,426,000 tokens/sec ≈ 12,509 QPS (15s headroom).

Suggested headroom targets (15s window) by region - quick table (rounded):
- us-west: 1.0M tokens/sec (headroom target) / est GPU mix: 7 H100 eq.
- us-east: 1.6M tokens/sec / 11 H100 eq.
- eu-central: 900k tokens/sec / 7 A100 eq.
- apac-northeast: 1.425M tokens/sec / 12 H100 eq.
- apac-southeast: 600k tokens/sec / 6 mixed eq.

Runbook (operational playbook - condensed):
Pre-burst (proactive):
- Maintain short-window (15s, 1m) alerting on tokens/sec and hot-model ratio. Alert thresholds: warn=p99.5, crit=p99.9 for 15s.
- Warm pool: keep N hot replicas (model-specific) pinned in each AZ for top-5 models. N = ceil(peak_cards_per_region * 0.12).
- Preload KV caches for top chat models during high-risk windows (marketing, major events).

During-burst (automated actions):
- If 15s crit threshold breached -> immediately enable admission control for non-critical endpoints (embeddings batch, rerank).
- Trigger cross-region shallow spill: route 10-30% of new sessions to designated backup region with compatible model variants.
- Autoscale: fast-path: allocate spare GPU slices (H100 from cold pool) using pre-approved capacity; fallback path: multiplex onto A100 with quantized variant.

Post-burst (after action):
- Run burst replay in replay-cluster to validate allocation sufficiency.
- Create incident note with top model IDs, sequence lengths, and traffic source tags.
- Evaluate whether safety multiplier should be increased for that region.

Experiments to run (next 6 weeks):
- Replay real 15s-peaks in the staging replay rig; validate per-GPU token throughput under 15s stress. Jira: JIRA-INFRA-1427.
- A/B test safety multipliers 1.10 vs 1.15 on historical peaks to measure unnecessary overprovisioning.
- Run synthetic concentrated-model bursts (top-1 model at 80%) to see routing fallout.

Open questions / risks:
- How representative is sampled event stream for 15s tails? We may be undercounting due to sampling. Action: increase raw retention to 30 days at full fidelity for a 4-week experiment.
- Model variant compatibility across regions: some regions do not have quantized variants; we need a mapping table.
- Billing/commit impact for spinning up cold H100 slices for microbursts. Need finance ops input for emergency burn rate.

Action items (owners):
- Maya Chen: schedule replay tests and collect per-card throughput numbers (due 2026-11-24).
- Arjun Patel: implement 15s sliding-window pipeline and dashboard (data infra) (PR target 2026-11-22).
- Lucia Gomez: add routing policy for shallow spill and draft fallback model mapping (2026-11-26).
- SRE oncall: draft incident response steps for peakhunt alerts (2026-11-20).

Appendix: quick notes and heuristics
- Use 15s sliding windows with 5s steps (captures narrow peaks but still smooths noise).
- Prefer p99.9 for 15s; p99 for 1m; p95 for 5m when deciding long-term capacity commitments.
- Safety multipliers: start conservative (1.15) for regions with intermittent big customers, use 1.05 for stable enterprise customers with reserved capacity.

Raw analysis snippets (copied outputs):
- apac-northeast: 15s_p99.9=1240000, median=95000, peak_model_conc=0.62
- us-east: 15s_p99.9=1380000, median=110k, peak_model_conc=0.48

Notes to self:
- This doc intentionally operational rather than final. We expect iterative improvements and more rigorous backtesting before elevating to "final".
- When elevating, fold in cost estimates per emergency H100 hour and expected frequency to recommend reserve commitments.

References and useful links:
- replay harness repo: github.com/redwood-inference/replay-harness (internal)
- historic event export: gs://redwood-infra/event-streams/2026/ (restricted)
- Slack thread: #infra-peakhunt (pin: Nov 8 discussion)

End of doc.
